title: Whiteboard 50s: quick wins for SE + sellers (wip)
content:
Purpose: a 6-slide, speaker-note driven pack of 50-second whiteboard narratives SEs and sellers can use in discovery or exec meetings. Not a formal deck — intentionally sketchy, focused on crisp metaphors + 1-2 numbers that land.

Slide 1 — One-liner opener (30–50s script)
- Visual: tiny 3-box drawing: app -> Redwood API -> model pools (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Script: "We serve models like a CDN serves media: same API, different capacity tiers — pick the mix that keeps your users fast and your bill predictable."
- Quick stat to pull: typical prefix cache reduces token cost by ~20–40% on chat flows (customer benchmark).
- Note to SE: Start by asking about concurrency and SLA needs before you sketch.

Slide 2 — The latency trade frame (whiteboard map)
- Visual: two-axis sketch (latency vs cost) with three pins: Hosted (low time-to-value), Dedicated (predictable throughput), Private (control/SLA).
- Talking points: "If they care <150ms p50, go dedicated or colocated private. If they care about time-to-market and lower ops, show Hosted plus fallback policy."
- Quick pull: known customers with routed fallbacks cut incident blast radius by 70% (anecdotal). Flag as "ask for later evidence" if challenged.

Slide 3 — Fault-tolerant picture: the fallback ladder (60s)
- Visual: ladder of fallback options: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> smaller model -> canned safe response -> retry region.
- Script bullets: "We build in graceful degradation so your product stays up. You can define per-route fallbacks and SLOs so customer-facing flows never block."
- SE cue: draw lines indicating OSS quantized models vs Redwood-verified models; call out SLA tiers.

Slide 4 — Sample 50s sketch for an integration (refund bot)
- Context: consumer app with chat and a refund workflow requiring 200 token prompt + 50 token response.
- Sketch labels: expected qps, latency target, sensitive data flag.
- Sell point: show an autoscale + burst plan and prefix caching to make cost predictable during spikes.
- Quick numbers to say: "We can approximate cost impact: ~0.01–0.03 $/session depending on quantization & cache hit rate." (calibrate with product team if pushed)

Slide 5 — Talking cards (pick 1–2 depending on audience)
- Technical buyer (platform/infra): emphasize deterministic throughput, GPU isolation, canary rollout hooks, observability traces. One-liner: "Pin model versions, roll forward with A/B canaries, roll back in minutes."
- Product/PM: emphasize latency-to-value, user experience continuity, and progressive rollouts. One-liner: "Keep your flows responsive even under load with automatic fallbacks and prefix caching."
- Legal/security exec: emphasize VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. One-liner: "You keep keys and logs, we run the inference."

Slide 6 — Quick workshop / next-steps template (for pilots)
- 3-minute checklist to leave with the customer:
  1) Target flows (name + example prompt)
  2) Latency & QPS targets (p50/p95 & burst qps)
  3) Data sensitivity classification (PII? regulated?)
  4) Desired rollout (canary % and fallback policy)
  5) Success metric (cost per 1k requests, latency SLA, user satisfaction)
- Leave-behind: small hand-drawn card (scan/photo) we can send to buyer afterwards.

Speaker notes / execution tips (internal):
- Keep it visual — draw boxes and arrows, avoid full sentences on the whiteboard.
- Use 1 concrete number point per meeting (latency or cost) — too many numbers dilutes.
- If pressed on pricing, defer to usage calc but give a directional band and offer a follow-up calc using their sample trace.
- If they ask about model parity vs vendor X, pivot to operational guarantees and rollback/fallback economics rather than raw benchmark claims.

Open items / follow-ups:
- Get an up-to-date cache hit % for chat templates from engineering (owner: Priya).
- Create 2 variant leave-behind PNGs: exec one-pager + engineer quick-checklist (owner: Jonah).
- Validate the "0.01–0.03 $/session" cadence with product pricing (Diego).

Notes-to-self: rough, hand-drawn aesthetic is okay here — the goal is fast persuasion and repeatable verbal scripts. Keep this under 2 pages when we publish a tidy version.

Related artifacts (for later linking):
- Pilot checklist google sheet (template) — add sheet id here after creation.
- Example canary traces and trace dashboard — ask Observability team for two sample dashboards to screenshot.

End-of-file: this is intentionally short. Use as a living sketch: drop quick wins and anecdotes here as SEs report back.
